children: The South African rand held steady on Tuesday as traders shrugged off a second-quarter economic contraction — its first in almost two years — driven by the Iran war's hit to domestic demand as well as weakness in the mining and manufacturing sectors.
At 1300 GMT, the rand traded at 15.9950 against the dollar
, little changed from its previous close.

Gross domestic product contracted 0.2% on a seasonally adjusted quarter-on-quarter basis (ZAGDPN=ECI), data from Statistics South Africa showed. Economists polled by Reuters had forecast a 0.1% contraction.
Economists said the weak reading reflected the hit from higher energy costs following the Iran war, but stopped short of calling it the start of a prolonged downturn.

"The evidence points to an economy in which recovery has been interrupted and delayed, rather than definitively derailed," said Prof Raymond Parsons, economist at North-West University Business School.

"Overall, the second quarter's GDP reading reflects a fragile domestic economy, constrained by high fuel costs as the ongoing situation in the Middle East has exacerbated the country's weak growth on structural impediments," said Investec economist Lara Hodes.
Focus will now turn to the current account (ZACACT=ECI), mining (ZAMNG=ECI) and manufacturing (ZAMAN=ECI) figures on Thursday for further clues on the health of Africa's most industrialised economy.
On the Johannesburg Stock Exchange, the Top-40 index
South Africa's benchmark 2035 government bond (ZAR2035=) weakened, with the yield up 5 basis points to 8.625%.
